Description: SWE-bench Verified evaluates software engineering ability by giving a model a real GitHub repository issue and requiring it to produce a patch that passes the project’s tests. The Verified subset consists of tasks that have been human-validated as solvable and have reliable evaluation harnesses, reducing noise from ambiguous or broken tasks.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: SWE-bench Multilingual extends the SWE-bench paradigm beyond Python to multiple programming languages, assessing whether models can debug and implement fixes across varied ecosystems and tooling. It emphasizes generalizable program understanding rather than language-specific memorization.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: SWE-bench Pro is a larger and more difficult set of software engineering tasks designed to be more realistic and more resistant to contamination than earlier SWE-bench variants. Tasks typically require deeper codebase understanding, multi-step debugging, and careful patch construction under stricter evaluation.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Decision-making (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: Terminal-Bench 2.0 evaluates agentic performance in a command-line environment, where a model must use shell commands and tooling to complete real tasks (e.g., debugging, data processing, environment setup). It stresses iterative interaction, tool use, and recovery from errors under realistic constraints.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory
L3: Cognitive Flexibility, Inhibitory Control (minor), Self-reflection (minor)

Description: BrowseComp evaluates web-browsing research capability by asking models to answer questions that require searching, reading, and synthesizing information from web documents. Performance depends on selecting relevant sources, tracking evidence, and producing grounded final answers.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension
L2: Planning, Attention, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: τ2-bench measures an agent’s ability to complete multi-turn customer-support-style tasks by interacting with simulated users and APIs while adhering to domain policies. It probes reliable tool calling, policy compliance, and coherent dialogue management over extended interactions.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Production (minor)
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory
L3: Social Reasoning & Theory of Mind, Inhibitory Control

Description: OSWorld benchmarks multimodal “computer use” in a desktop-like environment, requiring models to interpret screenshots and execute actions (clicking, typing, navigating) to accomplish tasks. It emphasizes robust GUI understanding, action sequencing, and long-horizon interaction.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Visual Attention & Eye Movements, Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory (minor)

Description: ARC-AGI-2 is a few-shot abstract reasoning benchmark where models infer the transformation rule from small sets of input–output grid examples and generate the correct output for new inputs. It is intended to measure fluid reasoning and adaptation to novel tasks rather than knowledge recall.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception (minor)
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Spatial Representation & Mapping, Planning (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: Vending-Bench 2 evaluates long-horizon autonomy by having an agent run a simulated vending-machine business over an extended period, optimizing purchasing, pricing, inventory, and communication. Success requires maintaining coherent goals and strategies across many steps and delayed outcomes.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Reward Mechanisms (minor), Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition (minor)
L3: Self-reflection (minor)

Description: MCP-Atlas evaluates real-world tool use via the Model Context Protocol, requiring models to discover tools, invoke them correctly, handle errors, and compose multi-step workflows across MCP servers. It focuses on reliable API interaction and orchestration rather than purely text-only reasoning.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory
L3: Cognitive Flexibility, Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: FinanceAgent assesses whether a model can complete tasks typical of an entry-level financial analyst, such as interpreting financial documents, building analyses, and producing structured recommendations. It emphasizes quantitative reasoning, domain knowledge, and producing decision-relevant outputs.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Production (minor)
L2: Logical Reasoning, Decision-making, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Working Memory, Planning (minor)

Description: CyberGym evaluates cybersecurity agent capability on large suites of tasks involving vulnerability identification and, in some settings, vulnerability discovery in real open-source projects. It tests whether models can reason about code, systems behavior, and exploit-relevant conditions under realistic constraints.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Planning, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor), Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: SpreadsheetBench evaluates the ability to understand, edit, and compute with complex spreadsheets, often requiring multi-step transformations and correct use of formulas and formatting. It targets practical productivity skills where small mistakes can cascade into incorrect final artifacts.
Cognitive Functions:

It is frequently evaluated both with and without tools (e.g., web search, code execution) to separate base competence from tool-augmented performance.

Description: AIME 2025 consists of competition mathematics problems from the American Invitational Mathematics Examination, requiring exact answers and multi-step derivations. It is commonly used to measure mathematical reasoning robustness and error-avoidance under pressure for correctness.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Planning (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: GPQA Diamond is a high-quality subset of GPQA composed of very difficult graduate-level science multiple-choice questions designed to be resistant to simple web lookup. It measures scientific reasoning and knowledge where distractors are strong and shallow pattern-matching tends to fail.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Working Memory (minor), Decision-making (minor)

Description: MMMLU extends MMLU to multiple languages, testing broad academic knowledge and reasoning across many subjects and non-English settings. It is used to assess multilingual generalization and whether reasoning performance transfers across languages rather than being English-centric.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor)

Description: MMMU is a multimodal benchmark requiring models to answer questions that combine images and text across diverse disciplines (e.g., science, engineering, charts, diagrams). It targets integrated visual understanding and reasoning rather than standalone OCR or captioning.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Multisensory Integration, Logical Reasoning (minor), Visual Attention & Eye Movements (minor)

Description: MMMU-Pro is a harder, more rigorously constructed variant of MMMU aimed at reducing shortcut solutions and better differentiating frontier multimodal models. It typically increases reasoning depth demands on diagrams, charts, and scientific imagery with more challenging questions and evaluation practices.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Multisensory Integration, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: LAB-Bench FigQA evaluates whether models can interpret and reason about scientific figures from biology papers, including plots, microscopy images, and schematic diagrams. It focuses on extracting the correct scientific meaning from visual evidence and linking it to the question context.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Multisensory Integration (minor), Attention (minor)

Description: WebArena evaluates autonomous web agents completing realistic tasks across multiple websites (e-commerce, forums, code hosting, maps) using browser interactions. It emphasizes robust navigation, form filling, state tracking, and recovery from mistakes in dynamic interfaces.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Visual Attention & Eye Movements, Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: MathArena Apex is a curated set of high-difficulty math problems used to compare frontier models’ mathematical reasoning, often with strict grading and competition-style questions. It is designed to stress deep multi-step derivations and consistency across diverse math topics.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Planning (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: ScreenShot-Pro evaluates understanding of high-resolution GUI screenshots from professional software contexts, requiring models to answer questions grounded in the interface layout and visual details. It probes fine-grained visual grounding and spatially aware interpretation rather than generic image captioning.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Visual Attention & Eye Movements, Spatial Representation & Mapping (minor), Working Memory (minor)

Description: CharXiv Reasoning asks models to answer questions about charts and figures (often from scientific papers), requiring extraction of quantitative/relational information and correct interpretation of axes, legends, and plotted trends. L1: Visual Perception

L1: Visual Perception

L3: Cognitive Timing & Predictive Modeling (minor)

Description: LiveCodeBench Pro evaluates coding ability on competitive-programming-style tasks with careful leakage controls, often scoring via pass@1 or Elo-style ratings. It emphasizes algorithmic problem solving under time/complexity constraints rather than repository-specific patching.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Planning, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: The FACTS Benchmark Suite systematically evaluates factuality and grounding by measuring whether model outputs are supported by given sources and whether they avoid hallucinated details. It targets reliability in information-sensitive settings rather than pure task completion.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Attention (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control, Self-reflection (minor)

Description: SimpleQA Verified is a factual question answering benchmark with verification procedures intended to improve label quality and reduce ambiguous items. It is used to test whether models can give correct, concise answers without confabulation.

L1: Language Comprehension
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: Global PIQA evaluates physical commonsense reasoning across many languages and cultural contexts, focusing on which actions or outcomes are physically plausible in everyday situations. It probes whether models generalize intuitive physics-like constraints beyond English-only benchmarks.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning, Spatial Representation & Mapping (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor)

Description: MRCR v2 (8-needle) tests long-context retrieval and multi-round co-reference by inserting multiple similar “needle” requests into long “haystacks” and asking the model to reproduce the correct response for a specified needle. It stresses sustained context integration and resistance to interference from distractor-similar content.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Working Memory, Attention, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Episodic Memory (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: GDPval evaluates well-specified professional knowledge work across many occupations by having models produce real work artifacts (e.g., spreadsheets, presentations, plans) that are judged against expert performance. It is designed to measure economically valuable task execution, often under tool-augmented workflows.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Production
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition
L3: Self-reflection (minor)

Description: SWE-Lancer evaluates end-to-end software engineering skill on realistic tasks that resemble contracted engineering work, typically requiring understanding requirements, making code changes, and validating behavior. It aims to measure practical engineering competence beyond narrow algorithm problems.
